blocks.text: Appendix C - Verified external resources

These resources support the course; They don't replace him. Each tab indicates recipients, level, advantages, limits, cost and way of use. All information has been checked on the pages indicated as source on 17–18 October 2026 . Prices, editions and availability change: check them again before buying. When a cost was not indicated in a reliable source, the card says so. How to choose. For A1 Just a manual in English to use as the second source of exercises and listening, Anki and a tutor. Consultation grammars and dictionaries become useful especially by A2. Resources with authentic materials (news, videos) serve A1 only in the lowest levels.
C1 · Manuals in English
Communicate in Arabic · Levels A1-A2
Monica Ruocco, Luca D'Anna, Souzan Fatayer · Hoepli, Necklace Oriental Studies, 2022 · ISBN 9788820399108 (paper), 9788836009763 (digital).
• Recipients: italophones beginners who study Arabic standard, alone or in a course.
• Level: A1-A2; First volume of a course in three volumes (A2-B1 in 2023Then B1-B2).

• Benefits: 15 Themed units (the first three on the writing system), dialogues and graduated texts, various exercises type with reviews, cultural and dialectal notes, thematic glossary; MP audio3 downloadable.
• Limits: teacher material is reserved; additional content requires code registration.
• Cost: € 34,90 paper; € 28,99 digital (platform HoepliAcademy+), publisher's prices.

• Use during the course: second source of exercises and listening for the topics of A1 (presenting, family, origin, food, market). Use it after the corresponding unit of this volume, not instead of it.
• Source: hoeplieditore.it
Contemporary Arabic Language · Grammar, Vocabulary and Exercises
Claudia Maria Tresso · Hoepli, 2publishing, 2019 · ISBN 9788820390778.
• Recipients: Italianophone students; the publisher presents it as ... expressly designed for students Italophones.
• Level: A1-B1.

• Benefits: 23 lessons in 5 units, each with grammar, vocabulary, exercises and texts (often dialogues), all vocalized and some even without vowels; 34 Conjugation tables; dictionary of about 800 vowels in both senses; MP audio3.
• Limits: covers three levels, then a A1 only the first part is used; is the most expensive of English manuals This list.
• Cost: € 47,90 paper; € 39,99 epub (Publisher's prices).
• Use during the course: additional exercises on the structures A1 and, by A2, on verbs; the conjugation tables complete Part V.
• Source: hoeplieditore.it
Arabic grammar · Manual of modern Arabic with exercises, vol. 1
Luc-Willy Deheuvels, Italian edition edited by Antonella Ghersetti · Zanichelli, Lingua necklace in practice, 2010 · ISBN 9788808162984.
• Targets: beginners who want a structured method to read, write and understand the standard Arabic.
• Level: beginner (volume 1 is the first part of the method; dealer card does not indicate a level
CEFR.
• Advantages: proven method (French original of 1993), adapted for italophones; financial years; 2 MP audio CD3;
indicated as a reference manual in the Arabic language programme 1 University Ca' Foscari of Venice (a.y. 2024/25).
• Limits: edition of the 2010; audio support on CD.
• Cost: € 33,30 cover price indicated by libreriauniversitya.it.
• Use during the course: consolidation exercises and reading texts; useful if you prefer a university approach.
• Sources: libreriauniversitya.it · programma Ca' Foscari
C2 · Grammars for consultation
Grammar of modern standard Arabic · Phonology, morphology and syntax
Giuliano Mion, Luca D'Anna · Hoepli, 2021 · ISBN 9788820385767.
• Recipients: students from beginner to advanced who want a complete grammar in English.
• Level: consultation, A1 Then.
• Advantages: it covers phonetics and writing, morphology of the name and verb, pronouns, numerals, syntaxes of sentence; recent.
• Limits: is a grammar of consultation, not a course; the publisher's card does not mention any exercises.
• Cost: € 39,90 paper; € 32,99 epub (Publisher's prices).
• Use in the course: when an explanation of units is not enough, look for the same topic here. From A2 becomes the main reference for morphology.
• Source: hoeplieditore.it
Theoretic-practical grammar of the Arabic language, vol. 1
Laura Veccia Vaglieri · Institute for the East C.A. Nallino, reprint 2011 · ISBN 9788897622017.
• Recipients: who wants the classic grammar of reference of Italian tradition.
• Level: consultation, A2 Then.
• Advantages: accuracy and completeness; revised exercises.
• Limits: work born in the thirties and here reprinted; according to the dealer's card the introductory part on the alphabet has few exercises.
• Cost: € 50,00 cover price indicated by libreriauniversitya.it.
• Use during the course: optional; useful later for syntax.
• Source: university library.it
C3 · Manuals in English
Mastering Arabic 1
Jane Wightwick, Mahmoud Gaafar · Bloomsbury, 4publishing, 2024 · ISBN 9781350367265.
• Recipients: absolute beginners who read English.
• Level: beginner; introduces writing from the front page.
• Benefits: 20 unity on daily themes (family, work, places, numbers, food, past, routine), with reviews in units 8, 15 and 20; free online audio and video.
• Limits: explanations in English; variable price according to the dealer.
• Cost: variable according to the dealer; I didn't find a price for the verifiable publisher.
• Use during the course: source of free additional listening on the topics of A1.
• Source: Book card at Abbey's Bookshop
Al-Kitaab fii Taʿallum al-ʿArabiyya · Part One
Kristen Brustad, Mahmoud Al-Batal, Abbas Al-Tonsi · Georgetown University Press, 3in the edition.
• Recipients: students of university courses, especially in the United States; English speakers.
• Level: beginner (first volume of the course).
• Advantages: accompanying site (Lingco platform) with audio, video and integrated exercises, in part with automatic correction also for those who study alone.
• Limits: in English; the accompaniment site is paid and is designed especially for courses with Teacher.
• Cost: USD 59,95 the access card to the accompanying site, according to the publisher's page; price of the unverified book.
• Use during the course: optional; It only makes sense if you take a course that takes it.
Source: press.georgietown.edu
C4 · Dictionaries
Arabic Dictionary · Italian-Arabic, Arabic-Italian
Eros Baldissera · Zanichelli, 2publishing, 2014.
• Recipients: Italophone students who already know the alphabet and the basics of grammar; translators.
• Level: A2 onward; a A1 Just the volume vocabulary.

• Advantages: approx. 46.000 voices and meanings; and 9.000 locutions; Modern, technical, legal and social vocabulary political; clear Italian-Arab section; indicated as a reference dictionary in the Arabic language programme 1 by Ca' Foscari (a.y. 2024/25).

• Limits: does not cover dialects; the Arabic-Italian section is less rich than the great specialist vocabularies; on grammatical summary is not suitable for beginners (from the review by Isabella Camera d'Afvolto on Translate).
• Cost: the review reports € 56,00 for paper and € 33,90 for the ebook; are prices of the time, from I'm gonna check again.
• Use during the course: from Level A2, to search for words by root and verify the plural.
• Sources: review on Translate · program Ca' Foscari
A Frequency Dictionary of Arabic · Core Vocabulary for Learners
Tim Buckwalter, Dilworth Parkinson · Routledge, 2011 · ISBN 9780415444347.
• Targets: who wants to know what words to study first.
• Level: A1 a B2.
• Benefits: 5.000 more frequent words than standard Arabic, in order of frequency, with example phrase, usage data and distribution indication in the main dialects; root index; Thematic lists.
• Limits: in English; is not a general consultation dictionary.
• Cost: The publisher's page did not show the price at the time of verification.
• Use during the course: to decide which words to add to Anki in addition to the vocabulary of units.
Source: routedge.com
C5 · Tools
Anki
• Target group: all.
• Level: all.
• Advantages: deferred repetition; Import course CSV files (Level bunches) 0 and Level A1); exists for computers, Android and iOS.
• Limits: requires daily constancy; arrears grow fast if you skip days (see recovery rules of the Plan).
• Cost: free computer version (Windows, macOS, Linux); AnkiDroid for free Android;
AnkiMobile for paid iOS (USD 24,99 on the US App Store; in Italy the price is in euros and may differ).
• Use during the course: every day, 10–20 minutes.
• Sources: apps.ankiweb.net · App Store
Forvo
• Targets: those who want to hear a word spoken by a native speaker.
• Level: all.
• Advantages: free; judgments recorded by native speakers; You don't need to register to listen.
• Limits: content inserted by users, so not always standard: many words are spoken in dialect;
Check the source of the speaker.
• Cost: free.
• Use during the course: punctual control of words of the vocabulary, not systematic study.
Source: European Centre for Modern Languages (ECML)
Voice summary for scripts

The catalog does not indicate a specific app: at the date of verification I did not find official sources that confirm, for a precise app, the support of Arabic vowels. If you use the voice synthesis of your phone or browser, choose an Arabic voice (not an Italian voice reading Arabic), try using the script of A1-01 and compare the result with the tutor. Remember the limits indicated in the Guide: final vowels, endings and some consonants can be read badly.
C6 · Listening and reading
Aswaat Arabiya
University of Texas at Austin (LAITS), published as an educational resource opened by COERLL.
• Recipients: Arabic students who want authentic listening with guided activities.
• Level: six levels, from Novice to Superior (ACTFL scale); a A1 Novice materials only.
• Advantages: authentic passages (legal, interviews, announcements, presentations of native speakers) from Morocco, Egypt,
Syria, Lebanon, Emirates and Qatar; Each unit has activities before, during and after listening; mostly Arabic standard.
• Limits: some intermediate passages contain dialect; the page does not say if the site is still up to date.
• Cost: open educational resource; The COERLL page contains the Creative Commons BY License.
• Use during the course: from the end A1, a song Novice per week; from A2 Then, regularly.
Sources: laits.utexas.edu/aswaat · coerll.utexas.edu
Al Jazeera Learning Arabic
• Recipients: students of Arabic standard, especially those interested in media language.
• Level: seven levels, from Introductionory to Proficiency; a A1 Introductionory and Beginner levels.
• Advantages: free; section "News in Levels" with graduated news by level and topic (policy, economy, culture, science...); grammar; level test; Vocation titles.
• Limits: many contents date back to 2021–2022; the page does not describe in detail the exercises; high levels assume B1 and beyond.
• Cost: free.
• Use during the course: from the end A1, news of the lowest levels as extra reading; from B1 is one of the main resources for media language.
Source: learning.aljazeera.net
C7 · Tutor and certification
Italki (Tutor Lessons)
• Recipients: who is looking for an online native language teacher for conversation, pronunciation and correction of productions.
• Level: all.
• Advantages: at the date of verification the site listed 393 Arabic tutor; each profile indicates the varieties spoken (for e.g. Arabic (Modern Standard), Egyptian, Gulf, Maghrebino; test lessons.
• Limits: quality depends on the individual teacher; the profiles are not certified by the course; Not all tutors teach standard Arabic; The payments are in dollars.
• Cost: determined by each teacher; according to frequent site questions, usually from USD 5 USD 50 The time.
• Use during: 1–2 sessions per week from A1, and oral tests of the test and examination. Choose a tutor who indicate the standard Arabic and ask it to use the directory of the Guide.
Source: italki.com
CIMA · Certificat international de maîtrise en arabe
Institut du monde arabe (IMA), Paris.
• Targets: those who want an external and independent feedback of their standard Arabic level.
• Level: six levels CEFR, from A1 a C2.

• Advantages: four tests (oral and written understanding with 44 multiple choice questions each, written production with three tasks, individual oral production of maximum 11 minutes); more than fifty centres in about twenty countries , including Italy; valid certificate 3 years; no licence required, minimum age 15 years; may be repeated after at least 60 days.
• Limits: the texts of the reading test are not vocized; dates and locations depend on the centers.
• Cost: determined by the examination centre; the candidate's guide does not indicate a price.
• Use during the course: recommended at the end of A2, B2 and C1 (Plan, section 6.4). It doesn't work out. A1.
• Source: CIMA candidate's guide (IMA, October 2024)
